- AI sessions build scripts, flows and apps with AI in a workspace fork, with a live preview and a diff to review before deploying.
- Workspace roles decide what each team can author, and folders scope the resources, skills and MCP servers its AI can reach.
- Protection rulesets block direct deployment, so changes reach production only after an engineer reviews and deploys them.
- Dev workspaces keep their own credentials, and promote to prod through Compare & Deploy or a Git pull request.
- Worker groups run AI-built code on its own workers, or on a separate instance.
See let business teams build with AI safely for the full setup. Engineers keep writing code locally with the CLI, the VS Code extension and their coding agent, synced with Git.

1. Define a minimal and generic script in Python, TypeScript, Go or Bash that solves a specific task. The code can be defined in the provided Web IDE or synchronized with your own GitHub repo (e.g. through VS Code extension): provided Web IDE or synchronized with your own GitHub repo (e.g. through VS Code extension):
2. Your scripts parameters are automatically parsed and generate a frontend.
3. Make it flow! You can chain your scripts or scripts made by the community shared on WindmillHub.
4. Build complex UIs on top of your scripts and flows.
Scripts and flows can be triggered by schedules, webhooks, HTTP routes, Kafka, WebSockets, emails, and more.
Flows can also be built in the visual flow editor or as YAML, with scripts like the first one as steps. See workflows as code.
- Data tables give each workspace managed Postgres tables, queried with type-checked SQL from TypeScript, Python and DuckDB scripts without exposing a connection string.
- DuckDB scripts query S3 and Azure Blob files (CSV, Parquet, JSON), data tables, Postgres, MySQL and BigQuery in SQL, on your workers.
- DuckLake stores large datasets as lakehouse tables in your workspace object storage, queried in plain SQL.
- Pipelines (alpha) wire scripts by the data they read and write instead of a hand-drawn DAG. This script runs whenever `events` is materialized, and materializes its own table:
Existing dbt projects run unmodified as scripts. See the pipelines quickstart.
|**CLI**|Sync a workspace with local files and Git, run scripts and flows from the command line. `wmill init` generates `AGENTS.md` and skill files for Claude Code, Cursor and other AI tools|
|**VS Code extension**|Edit and test scripts and flows from VS Code or Cursor with full IDE support|
|**Git sync**|Two-way sync between a workspace and your Git repository|
|**MCP server**|Let coding agents and AI clients run scripts, manage resources and monitor jobs in a workspace|
|**AI sessions**|The same agent loop in the browser, with nothing to install: plan mode, skills and MCP servers, a live preview, and a diff to review before deploying, in a fork of the workspace|
You can run scripts locally by passing the right environment variables for the `wmill` client library to fetch resources and variables from your instance. See local development docs.
- TypeScript/JavaScript: Bun (default); Deno only on the `windmill-full` images
- Python: python3 with uv for dependency management
- Go, Bash, PowerShell, Rust, C#, Java, Ansible
- **Sandboxing**: nsjail for filesystem/resource isolation, and PID namespace isolation (enabled by default) to prevent jobs from accessing worker process memory

Windmill architecture: business teams and engineers build through stateless API servers into workspaces, where changes move from dev and forks to prod after review. PostgreSQL holds the job queue and state. Worker groups for dev and prod, native workers and remote agent workers pull jobs by tag and reach your databases, APIs and AI model providers.
For detailed setup options, see Self-Host documentation.
Configure OAuth and SSO (Google Workspace, Microsoft/Azure, Okta) directly from the superadmin UI. See documentation.
In Windmill, integrations are referred to as resources and resource types. Each Resource has a Resource Type that defines the schema that the resource
On self-hosted instances, you might want to import all the approved resource types from WindmillHub. A setup script will prompt you to have it being synced automatically everyday.
|MODE|standalone|The mode of the binary: standalone, server, worker, agent (EE), indexer (EE image, full-text search), mcp|All|
|WORKER_GROUP|default|The worker group the worker belongs to and gets its configuration pulled from|Worker|
|BASE_URL|http://localhost:8000|The base url that is exposed publicly to access your instance. Is overriden by the instance settings if any.|Server|
|LICENSE_KEY (EE only)|None|License key checked at startup for the Enterprise Edition of Windmill|Worker|
All other variables (database pool, queue, runtimes, private registries, certificates, zombie jobs and more) are documented in the environment variables reference.
> A curated list of awesome PostgreSQL software, libraries, tools and resources, inspired by awesome-mysql
PostgreSQL, often simply Postgres, is an object-relational database (ORDBMS). PostgreSQL is ACID-compliant and transactional. (see more: wikipedia:PostgreSQL, PostgreSQL.org)
:elephant: Contributions welcome. Add links through pull requests or create an issue to start a discussion. Please take a look at the contribution guidelines.
* autobase - Autobase for PostgreSQL® is an open-source DBaaS that automates the deployment and management of highly available PostgreSQL clusters.
* BDR - BiDirectional Replication - a multimaster replication system for PostgreSQL
* Patroni - Template for PostgreSQL HA with ZooKeeper or etcd.
* Spock - 100% open-source logical multi-master PostgreSQL replication.
* Stolon - PostgreSQL HA based on Consul or etcd, with Kubernetes integration.
* pglookout - Replication monitoring and failover daemon.
* repmgr - Open-source tool suite to manage replication and failover in a cluster of PostgreSQL servers.
* Slony-I - "Master to multiple slaves" replication system with cascading and failover.
* PAF - PostgreSQL Automatic Failover: High-Availibility for Postgres, based on Pacemaker and Corosync.
* SkyTools - Replication tools, including PgQ, a queuing system, and Londiste, a replication system a bit simpler to manage than Slony.
* pg_auto_failover - Postgres extension and service for automated failover and high-availability.
* pgrwl - Stream write-ahead logs (WAL) from a PostgreSQL server in real time. A drop-in, container-friendly alternative to pg_receivewal.
* pg-status - A microservice that provides HTTP endpoints for instantly retrieving the current master host or a replica that meets various criteria.
* Barman - Backup and Recovery Manager for PostgreSQL by 2ndQuadrant.

* pgbackweb - A Complete Docker-based Postgres backup and maintenance tool with Web UI.
* pg\_back - pg\_back is a simple backup script

agmsg is a thin transport. Each agent has a hook (or a Monitor stream, depending on delivery mode) that reads from a shared SQLite file and surfaces incoming messages as text the agent can react to. Sending is a `send.sh` call that appends a row. agmsg itself runs with no daemon, no socket and no broker — the file is the shared floor and the agents take turns on it. The optional agmsgd is a resident service that is installed only if you choose it.

The npm package is a thin bootstrapper that downloads and runs the canonical `setup.sh`. Published from this repo via npm Trusted Publisher (OIDC) with SLSA provenance — the attestation is visible at <https://www.npmjs.com/package/agmsg>.

|backendkiller|**Yes**: a single session grows backend RSS until OOM-kill and full instance restart; a very large `plan-size` makes each `PREPARE` heavy/slow|
|failconns|**Yes**: exhaust `max_connections` limit; this leads to other clients are unable to connect to Postgres|
|forkconns|**Yes**: excessive creation of Postgres child processes; potentially might lead to `max_connections` exhaustion|
|idlexacts|**Yes**: might lead to tables and indexes bloat|
|slotbloat|**Yes**: an un-consumed replication slot pins WAL; `pg_wal` grows until the filesystem is full, the instance can no longer write and PANICs|
|tempfiles|**Yes**: might increase storage utilization and degrade storage performance|
|terminate|**Yes**: already established database connections could be terminated accidentally|
|waitxacts|**Yes**: locks heavy-write tables; this leads to blocking concurrently executed queries|
|walflood|**Yes**: high-rate WAL generation drives replication lag and IO pressure; in a constrained environment `pg_wal` grows toward disk-full and the instance PANICs|
- `docs/workloads/backend-killer.md` — drive a single backend to OOM and an instance restart; cap memory, disable swap, and turn up the plan pressure.
- `docs/workloads/slot-bloat.md` — fill `pg_wal` with one forgotten replication slot until the disk is full; CLI flags, two stand recipes, and slot-crash recovery.
- `docs/workloads/wal-flood.md` — flood WAL with parallel `UPDATE`-churn workers; the honest env-dependent contract, the disk-full conditions, demo parameters, and how it differs from `slot-bloat`.

- `docs/workloads/bloat-churn.md` — outrun autovacuum by raw rate to grow remediable heap+index bloat; the trio that builds it, the post-stop repair reveal (`VACUUM FULL` / `pg_repack` / `REINDEX CONCURRENTLY`), what to watch via pgstattuple, and how a rate attack differs from `xmin-horizon-holder`'s horizon attack.

- `docs/workloads/tempfiles.md` — spill on-disk temp files by sorting a seeded dataset larger than `work_mem` on a default-configured server; how to watch `temp_files`/`temp_bytes` and `log_temp_files`, and the headline remediation — raise `work_mem` and the spill disappears.

- `docs/workloads/waitxacts.md` — build a pile of blocked waiter sessions behind one held table lock; the observation demo (a flickering staircase of `wait_event_type='Lock'`) and the cascade demo (unbounded waiters until `max_connections` is exhausted), plus the `superuser_reserved_connections` role trick that keeps a `postgres` monitor alive while `app` clients are refused.
